Think of a VPN as a private tunnel between your phone or laptop and the internet.

Normally, anyone along the way, like your Wi-Fi owner or your internet company, can see which sites you visit. With a VPN, everything you send is locked first, then travels through the tunnel to a VPN company's computer. That computer opens it and talks to the website for you.

So the website sees the VPN's address instead of yours, and the Wi-Fi owner only sees scrambled data. It helps on public Wi-Fi and hides your location a bit. It doesn't make you fully anonymous, since the VPN company can still see your activity.
